## free-tier-llm-landscape
- What matters: Groq, Together, OpenRouter, Gemini and Hugging Face all run free tiers with per-minute/per-day rate limits that change without notice; free model lists rotate, and OpenRouter's free models inherit the underlying provider's terms.
- Why it matters: an agent with no paid fallback can hard-fail on a limit change, a delisted model, or a ToS clause (attribution, no resale, no automated scraping) it never explicitly accepted.
- Verify: each provider's current limits and terms today, and whether your most-used model is still flagged free on OpenRouter.

## agent-safety-practice
- What matters: tiered approvals (auto-read, confirm-write, deny-destructive), sandboxing with network egress controls, treating all tool output as untrusted, and immutable audit logs of prompts, tool calls and diffs.
- Why it matters: autonomous coding agents touch secrets and repos; injection via issues, PRs and READMEs is the main breach path, and logs are the only way to reconstruct an incident.
